title: Grid
wrapsNative: LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:))], spacing:) for responsive tiles; LazyVGrid with flexible GridItems for a set number of columns; Grid with GridRow for aligned rows and columns
summary: A responsive grid is the standard LazyVGrid, and a table-like layout is the standard Grid, with spacing from the Monarch space scale. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: LazyVGrid with an adaptive GridItem for card grids and tiles: as many columns as fit items of a minimum width. Flexible GridItems for a set number of columns. Grid with GridRow for a small form or a key and value layout whose columns must line up.
whenNotToUse: For a single row that wraps use MonarchFlowLayout (see inline). For long, uniform, selectable rows use List.
api: LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem], alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, pinnedViews: PinnedScrollableViews = .init(), content: () -> Content)
GridItem(_ size: GridItem.Size = .flexible(), spacing: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment? = nil)
Grid(alignment: Alignment = .center, horizontalSpacing: CGFloat? = nil, verticalSpacing: CGFloat? = nil, content: () -> Content)
platformNotes: The web's Grid takes minItemWidth (default 16rem) or column counts per breakpoint, a gap from the space scale (default 16px) and fit or fill. On iOS minItemWidth is GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:)), which behaves like the web's fit: columns stretch to share the width. Columns per breakpoint become a count chosen from horizontalSizeClass. Pass theme.spacing values for the gaps; the column gap is set on the GridItem and the row gap on the grid. Android uses LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Adaptive.
accessibility: Layout only: no element is added. VoiceOver reads the items in source order, row by row.
Scale the minimum item width with @ScaledMetric so that fewer columns are used at large Dynamic Type sizes.
edgeCases: LazyVGrid creates items lazily only inside a ScrollView; elsewhere it lays out every item.
An adaptive minimum wider than the grid still gives one column, which then overflows; cap it with the available width if items can be that wide.
Grid is not lazy and sizes each column to its widest cell.
